problem: Zero-shot map-based object navigation handles only single-object or simple-label queries; queries with spatial relations ('remote on the table') are unsupported online, since prior spatial-query methods need offline 3D reconstruction or ignore relational constraints.
motivation: Human instructions often specify targets by spatial relations to other objects, and robots must resolve these during online exploration. CLIP-based semantic maps cannot encode complex language, while LVLMs alone lack the 3D reasoning for long-range navigation, so combining the two is attractive.
key_idea: Decompose a spatial query with an LVLM into simple proximity object queries, intersect their CLIP similarity maps with a continuous min operation to guide frontier exploration, and validate the candidate with an LVLM against the original constraint.
insight: Relaxing spatial relations to proximity lets a cheap semantic belief map (min-intersection blended with max) steer exploration toward co-existence regions, while the LVLM is used only sparingly for verification. This reduces false positives versus a primary-target-only baseline (FP 0.76 to 0.44 in sim; 40% to 0% real). There is no isolated ablation of the intersection module; the evidence is the comparison to OneMap given the same decomposed primary target and qualitative examples.
method: Decomposition: an onboard LVLM (Phi-4 multimodal) extracts explicit, inferred and implicit targets, the primary target, and their relations; only proximity relations (in/on/near) are kept, non-proximity ones (not in, far from) are discarded.
Semantic belief map: OneMap-style online 2D map of CLIP-aligned patch embeddings with uncertainty; each query gives a cosine-similarity map S_i.
Semantic intersection: S_int = min_i S_i over continuous values, no thresholds; Gaussian map blurring makes 'next to' overlap.
Combined map: S_comb = 0.9*S_int + 0.1*max_i S_i, so early exploration still has guidance; reduces to the single-object map if Q has one target.

Frontier/cluster navigation: frontiers scored by max S_comb in the unexplored region, clusters by peak S_comb; greedy selection with A* planning; detections are gated by a consensus filter (detector fires and cell in the top 5 percentile of S_comb).
LVLM validation: approach within 0.5 m, then the LVLM checks that the primary target is present and the original spatial constraint holds; otherwise continue search.

setting.backbone: Phi-4-multimodal (5.6B, frozen) for decomposition/validation; CLIP-aligned SED segmentation for the map; YOLOv7 / YOLO-World detectors (GPT-4o-mini also mentioned for real world)
setting.observation: posed RGB-D (256x256, 79° HFOV) with GPS+compass in sim; RealSense D455 RGB-D + Livox lidar Fast-LIO2 odometry on real robot
setting.action_space: discrete move forward 0.25 m, turn 15°, FOUND in sim; velocity commands via path tracker on Spot
setting.privileged: noiseless GPS+compass in the simulator; none otherwise

numbers.eval_set_note: minival split: 100 episodes, 3 sequential targets, 20 scenes
15 episodes x 3 targets (45 targets) in 4 indoor scenes; episodes not terminated on wrong found
numbers.backbone: Phi-4-multimodal (GPT-4o-mini used for part of the stack)
numbers.extra: SR per object; 40 of 45 targets found

numbers_note: MultiON values are printed as fractions (0-1) and copied as printed. No ablation tables are given.
results: On the MultiON minival split DIV-Nav gets SRAT 0.30, Pr 0.14, SR 0.04, beating OneMap (0.24/0.10/0.03) and the RL-trained IntelliGO Labs (0.23/0.10/0.03). On the real Spot it reaches 88% per-object success (40/45) versus 53% (24) for OneMap, with 0% vs 40% false positives.
limitations: Only proximity relations are supported; far from, between and directional relations are not, and unsatisfiable constraints lead to terminate-not-found.
The CLIP-based map struggles with small, occluded or fine-grained objects, and LVLM validation sometimes wrongly rejects correct detections.
Absolute simulation performance is very low (SR 0.04), the real-world evaluation is small (15 episodes), and there are no component ablations.
